newsitem.title: USA: UFO experts divided on truth of Roswell alien landing.
newsitem.headline: UFO experts divided on truth of Roswell alien landing.

text.p: UFO experts ridicule the Pentagon's official line on an alleged alien landing here 50 years ago, but they spend as much effort fighting among themselves over each and every detail of what really happened.

Where the alien spacecraft crashed, what its alien crew looked like and why they came are issues of bitter dispute between researchers and "witnesses" gathering this week to mark the 50th anniversary of the Roswell Incident.

Tens of thousands of people attending the UFO festival are being offered four separate "crash sites" and a string of exhibits and lectures that push conflicting theories on how many spacecraft and aliens crashed into the New Mexico desert, and what happened to them.

There is no physical evidence backing up any one version and eyewitness testimony, including that of a man who says he was making love with his girlfriend in the back of a pickup truck when they saw the spacecraft crash, is contradictory.
Each researcher has books to sell and they all compete for top billing at UFO conventions to justify their theories. Sometimes that means knocking their rivals.

"These guys spend more time attacking each other than focusing on what's really happening. They call each other liars, frauds, stupid ... It's crazy," UFO researcher Robert Dean said at the Roswell extravaganza late on Tuesday.
Most "experts" agree on two things: the aliens who landed in Roswell were not little green men, and the Pentagon is lying in order to cover up the incident.

The Air Force last week released a report saying that the alleged UFO wreckage found on a ranch northeast of here was in fact that of a top-secret military balloon used to monitor Soviet nuclear tests at the start of the Cold War.
The "aliens" reported by Roswell "witnesses" were most likely dummies used to test high-altitude parachutes a decade later in the late 1950s, the Air Force said.
Any hopes the Pentagon may have had that its report would calm the fervor of alien buffs were quickly quashed as indignant UFOlogists jumped to attack its findings.

"It's a bunch of baloney, it's a cover-up," said Robert Shirkey, who was assistant group operations officer at the Roswell Army Air Field in 1947 and says he saw the wreckage of the alien craft loaded onto a plane there.
But few believe the UFO community's brief united front against the Pentagon report will last long.
On even the basic issue of where the alien spacecraft allegedly landed, there are irreconcilable differences.

One witness said the craft put down at a ranch 75 miles (120 km) northwest of Roswell. Another said it was in a dry river bed about 40 miles (64 km) north of Roswell. A third said the landing spot was 55 miles (88 km) west of Roswell.
Their descriptions of the spacecraft range from a flying saucer to a bat-winged craft exactly like the U.S. military's B-2 stealth bomber.

The aliens themselves, the witnesses say, were either ash-coloured "good-looking people" about 5 feet 5 inches (1.65 meters) tall with fine features or under 4 feet (1.3 meters) tall, or "really funny-looking people" with great big eyes.
Kaufmann said he believed the aliens came in peace but other researchers have claimed they came to abduct humans or to gain intelligence on Earth's defences.
Critics point to the contradictions and the evidence provided by the military to conclude that researchers are simply barking up the wrong tree.

"Roswell is this giant dead red herring lying in the path of UFO research," said Karl Pflock, a researcher who believes extraterrestrial life may exist. "The legend, the myth, has taken on a life of its own, the facts don't matter anymore."
